slides.title: ~Rank~ rows
tip: Ravi and Karan both earn 61,000. RANK gives them 2 and 2, then jumps to 4.

rows.name: Number every row
rows.formula: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;

rows.name: Rank, ties share a place
rows.formula: SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;

rows.name: Rank with no gaps
rows.formula: SELECT name, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;

rows.name: Rank inside each dept
rows.formula: SELECT dept, name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;
rows.result: HR Neha 1, HR Sneha 2, IT Asha 1, ...

rows.name: Top earner per dept
rows.formula: WITH r AS (SELECT name, dept, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rk FROM employees) SELECT dept, name FROM r WHERE rk = 1;
rows.result: HR Neha, IT Asha, Sales Vikas

slides.data: Practice tables (example): employees (8 staff, 3 depts, salary), sales (North and South, Jan to Mar 2024), orders (8 orders, 4 customers).

slides.title: Running ~totals~
tip: GROUP BY squashes rows. OVER keeps every row and adds the total beside it.

rows.name: Running total by region
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, SUM(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) FROM sales;

rows.name: Region total on every row
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, SUM(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region) FROM sales;

rows.name: Share of region, %
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, ROUND(100.0 * sales / SUM(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region), 1) FROM sales;

rows.name: 3-month moving average
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, ROUND(AVG(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)) FROM sales;

rows.name: Dept average beside salary
rows.formula: SELECT name, salary, ROUND(AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept)) FROM employees ORDER BY id;

slides.title: Compare with ~last~ month
slides.ribbon: LAG and LEAD do the VLOOKUP-to-row-above for you
tip: LAG looks back, LEAD looks ahead. The first row has nothing behind it, so you get NULL.

rows.name: Previous month's sales
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, LAG(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) FROM sales;

rows.name: Month-on-month change
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, sales - LAG(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) FROM sales;

rows.name: Next month's sales
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, LEAD(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) FROM sales;

rows.name: First month as baseline
rows.formula: SELECT region, month, FIRST_VALUE(sales) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY month) FROM sales;

rows.name: Split staff into 4 pay bands
rows.formula: SELECT name, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;

slides.title: Interview ~classics~
slides.ribbon: Asked in almost every SQL round
tip: You cannot use a window function in WHERE. Wrap it in a CTE or subquery first.

rows.name: Second highest salary
rows.formula: SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM (SELECT salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dr FROM employees) WHERE dr = 2;

rows.name: Find duplicate emails
rows.formula: SELECT email FROM (SELECT email, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM employees) WHERE rn > 1;

rows.name: Latest order per customer
rows.formula: SELECT customer_id, order_date FROM (SELECT customer_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) AS rn FROM orders) WHERE rn = 1;

slides.title: Which one do I ~use~?
rows: A unique number on every row
Ties to share a rank, gaps after
Ties to share a rank, no gaps
SUM / AVG with ORDER BY inside OVER
A group total beside each row
SUM with PARTITION BY, no ORDER BY
ROW_NUMBER or RANK, then filter in a CTE
